evidence.claim: Laureate investor materials describe the company as operating five higher-education institutions across Mexico and Peru with approximately 500,000 students in undergraduate, graduate, and specialized degree programs.

Afya reported that 95.7% of 2025 revenue was generated by its Undergraduate and Continuing Education segment, primarily driven by monthly tuition fees charged to enrolled students.
Vitru reported that its student base exceeded 1.04 million in Q2 2025, with distance-learning undergraduate enrollment up 19.5% year over year.

evidence.claim: Duolingo's 2025 annual report source indicates paid subscriber penetration of 9% of MAUs as of December 31, 2025.
Duolingo's 2025 filing source says more than 6,100 education programs worldwide accepted Duolingo English Test results as of December 31, 2025.
Chegg reported Q2 2025 subscription-services subscribers of 2.6 million, down 40% year over year, and subscription-services revenue down 39% year over year.
Chegg's 2025 annual report source identifies Google AI Overviews as a factor that could continue to reduce traffic and accelerate declines in new subscriber sign-ups.

Pearson's 2025 annual report page says the company embedded AI more deeply across products and services and built momentum in enterprise through strategic partnerships, including Early Careers and Enterprise Skilling.

Wiley described itself as a provider of authoritative content, data-driven insights, and knowledge services for science and learning, and cited research publishing platform milestones and AI innovation in Q1 FY2026.
evidence.source_title: AI Demand Drives Wiley’s First Quarter 2026 Results

evidence.claim: Franklin Covey reported FY2025 consolidated subscription and subscription-services revenue of $225.9 million versus $231.8 million in FY2024.
evidence.source_title: Franklin Covey Reports Financial Results for Fourth Quarter and Full Fiscal 2025

evidence.source_title: Franklin Covey Reports First Quarter Fiscal 2025 Financial Results

evidence.claim: SLM's 2025 Form 10-K says its primary business is originating and servicing private education loans, with approximately $7.4 billion of private education loan originations in 2025, up 6% from 2024.
SLM reported that 92.8% of 2025 private education loans originated were cosigned and that the average FICO score at approval was 755.
Navient's 2025 10-K source says its total portfolio of private education loans was $15.5 billion and its FFELP loan portfolio was $28.1 billion as of December 31, 2025.
Navient's 2025 filing source says the company provided transition services related to outsourcing loan servicing and divesting the Business Processing segment.

memory_update.text: AFYA maps most directly to a Serenity-style chokepoint in this chunk because medical-school seats are regulator-authorized capacity and the company discloses 3,768 approved medical-school seats.
LAUR is an underfollowed international degree-capacity name tied to Mexico and Peru enrollment rather than U.S. Title IV dynamics; promote only after program mix and pricing evidence are verified.
VTRU remains speculative-shadow despite strong student-scale evidence because the public listing migrated from Nasdaq to B3 and current liquidity/market-cap accessibility must be verified.
DUOL should remain a reference leader for AI-native consumer learning and digital assessment, not the primary underfollowed lane.
CHGG is useful as a canary for AI-driven compression in search traffic and student-acquisition economics, with 2025 subscriber declines providing direct evidence of pressure.
PSO is a large-cap reference benchmark for assessment, credentials, enterprise skilling, and AI-enabled education content.
WLY may be better treated as academic-content and AI-licensing infrastructure than as a pure education ticker; segment disaggregation is required.
FC qualifies as an underfollowed workforce-training candidate because its subscription model and Education Division sit adjacent to employer and school leadership-development demand.
SLM is a reference indicator for education affordability and willingness to borrow; its exposure is credit and funding-cycle sensitive rather than a direct education-capacity chokepoint.
NAVI should remain speculative-shadow because its education exposure is dominated by managed/runoff loan portfolios, servicing transition, regulatory history, and credit provisions.
Need current market-cap, liquidity, analyst-coverage, institutional-ownership, and short-interest checks for LAUR, AFYA, VTRU3, CHGG, WLY, FC, SLM, and NAVI before Layer 3 prioritization.
Need program-level exposure for LAUR, AFYA, and VTRU: healthcare/STEM/business mix, online versus campus delivery, pricing, retention, graduation, employment outcomes, and regulatory approvals.
Need AI-impact comparison across DUOL, CHGG, PSO, and WLY: which firms monetize AI-enhanced learning or content licensing versus which face AI substitution and traffic compression.

summary: Layer 2B maps the candidate chunk into ticker-to-node relationships across international regulated degree capacity, healthcare/medical education seats, digital learning software, assessment/content, workforce training, and education finance. The underfollowed lane is strongest for AFYA, LAUR, VTRU, and FC because their exposure sits in regulated capacity or enterprise/workforce channels rather than headline edtech. DUOL, PSO, and SLM are primarily reference comparables. CHGG, WLY, and NAVI are speculative-shadow names useful for AI disruption, content licensing, or education-credit runoff read-through, but require stricter evidence before promotion.
